The government of Canada on Wednesday announced new measures to protect workers and companies impacted by higher tariffs imposed by the United States on aluminum and steel imports from the U.S.
The measures will also cover other sectors, including oil and natural gas - but in a release the Finance Department noted that there are no current plans for retaliatory duties on automotive products like cars and trucks.
Premier Doug Ford made clear in an interview with Bloomberg published on Tuesday that he would not use the tariffs to negotiate the US to lower the aluminum and steel tariffs.
A number of other provinces also have spoken out against trade war.

Canada is a major source of aluminum, iron and steel.
In the past the US imposed countervailing duties of up to 25% in 2025 on those imports from all Countries but the measures will be phased-in overtime.
The government warned the Canadian exporters could face significant disruption by the new US tariffs on some products like aluminum foil, that's made in Canada and US.

Premier Doug Ford also said the tariffs were a tax on US businesses, workers and consumers but he does not believe they are targeted at the American middle-class.
US President Donald Trump had imposed tariffs of 25% on Canadian steel and aluminum imports from China as a national security measure to protect US agriculture in 2025 but he said he will impose retaliatory measures if Canada does not remove its tariffs, that's what the U.S. is doing would be "a disaster".
